## Active

### D-848 — A committed blob has no expiry; the upload window is cleared at commit

> _2026-11-14 · realm/blong-blob · active_

`blob.upload.prepare` writes `expiresAt` because it reserves a key for a window in which bytes may
arrive, and `blob.upload.commit` used to keep it. That made a _stored_ photograph look expired to
`blob.temp.cleanup`, which asks only whether a record's `expiresAt` has passed — so the sweep
deleted committed blobs a day after their upload, and a test that committed and then read a record
saw it vanish between two steps. The commit now clears `expiresAt` for a record it does not mark
temporary: the window belongs to the upload, and a stored blob has no lifetime unless the caller
asked for one. The alternative — teaching the sweep to skip non-temporary records — was rejected
because it leaves two meanings of `expiresAt` in the records, and the sweep would still be reading a
field that lies.

### D-849 — Both stores answer one namespace: the orchestrator never names a backend

> _2026-11-14 · realm/blong-blob · active_

`blob` never names a backend in its handlers: every orchestrator call is
`storage.blob.put/get/head/find/ remove/meta.put`, dispatched to whichever store adapter the
configuration activates. So the object-store backend (T-665) declares the same
`namespace: 'storage'` and its group answers the same method names, and one process loads either
`blob.store` (cacache) or `blob.s3` (an S3-compatible bucket) — never both. The plan's draft names
(`s3StorePut` …) would have put the backend in the wire name and forced every caller to pick one,
which is the opposite of "the orchestrator picks a backend by config alone". The cost of this
choice: the folder under `adapter/s3/` carries files named `storageBlobPut.ts` and so on, which
reads oddly beside `s3.ts` — the alternative was renaming the six handlers the read and write paths
already call, in the same change as adding a backend.

### D-854 — The store declares one claim, namespaces separate the realms

> _2026-11-14 · realm/blong-blob · active_

D-845 gave every realm that owns blobs a claim of its own — `partyBlob`, `sportBlob` — and that is
not expressible: a k8s collection reaches the plan from a port's activation, the realms that own the
records (`party`, `sport`) own no port of their own (their handlers live on the shared `srv.subject`
and `srv.db`), and a suite's config block for a port does not carry `k8sVolumes` into the plan
either — tried both, and the generated sport tree came out without a volume. So the store declares
one claim, `blobStorage`, mounted at `/var/lib/blong/blob`, and the namespace is a subdirectory
inside it: two realms in one process share the claim and their files stay apart, and a split process
mounts the same claim and serves the namespace it was configured with. The consequence for an
operator is that one claim holds every realm's blobs rather than a claim per realm, which is what a
single directory per process was always going to mean. The ingress follows the same shape: one `/a`
on whichever deployment carries the process, rather than a rule per namespace.
